newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Rugby League club North Sydney's president Ray Beattie said the demise of the ARL was inevitable unless Optus Vision and Channel Nine offer another financial support package. Beattie said the competition could survive for the short-term without the support but would be heading for trouble in the long-term. Optus Vision and Channel Nine are expected to indicate today whether or not they will continue funding the competition. Page 18.

Super League should stay loyal to local referees who have supported the game, according to Super League referee Stephen Clarke. Clarke said it would not be fair to those referees who signed with the rebel competition and remained out of the game during th court proceedings, if others came in over the top of them. Super League said it had had calls from ARL referees since the court ruling was handed down. Page 18.

Sydney Swans defender Andrew Dunkley was suspended from the Australian Football League until the third round of next year's season. Dunkley faces suspension for striking Essendon's James Hird with a fist to the face. Dunkley denied the allegation but was nable to explain why his left arm made a swinging motion as he and Hird fell to the ground. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Rugby League club Parramatta confirmed it had been approached by the Penrith club about a possible merger. As ARL clubs wait patiently for the verdict on future funding for the competition, they are also talking mergers. Penrith president Roger Cowan said the possible merger could form a western Sydney super club. Page 40.

Following her success at the Metropolitan at Randwick yesterday, Australian horse trainer Gai Waterhouse was crowned the 'incredible lady' by Australian Jockey chairman Bob Charley. Waterhouse's horse Hula Flight won yesterday's Group 1 A$500,000 prize in what will be her third win at the Metropolitan in only four years as a trainer. Page 40.

The Australian Rugby Football Union's push to turn the Wallabies' seven-week trek through Europe into a grand slam tour has failed. The Union is giving up its efforts as the Home Unions would not budge in changing the date of the Barbarians match on Decemer 7 to allow a Test against England to act as the finale to the Wallaby tour. Page 39.
THE AGE

The National Basketball League's Brisbane Bullets went down to the too powerful Melbourne Tigers last night after they were defeated 96-87 at Melbourne Park. The win squared the best-of-three series for NBL's minor premiers, with the decider to be played tomorrow night at Melbourne Park. Page C8.

Despite his unexpected withdrawal from a qualifying tournament in Beijing over the weekend, Pat Cash remains on track to play at next year's Ford Australia Open. Claims Cash is not ready for a comeback and that his attempt will prove as unsuccessful as thse before have not dampened the hopes of the tennis star's father Pat Cash senior, who says his son is on track to play. Page C8.

Australian Football League wingman Scott Camporeale has turned down a lucrative deal with Port Power to stay with Carlton Football Club. Though the offer to return to Adelaide was tempting, Camporeale signed with Carlton for at least another three seasons citing his teammates as one of the reasons he decided to stay. Page C3.
HERALD SUN

Australian jockey Darren Beadman is almost certain to return to ride Saleous in the Caulfied Cup - news which saw her price tumble after word filtered to bookmakers. The pair has won three feature races including last Spring's Wakeful Stakes - Victoria Oasis double. Page 69.

The Australian Football League's Jason Dunstall looks set to play another year of football after he recovers from his recent knee reconstruction. Dunstall has been sidelined for six months but said the surgery went well and hoped to be playing again before the end of his contract - the end of 1997. Page 69.

Australian jockey Chris Munce will appeal against a suspension which has cost him his ride in the Caulfield Cup. Munce was to ride Gai Waterhouse's horse Hula Flights which has just won the Metropolitan at Randwick. Hula Flight is equal favourite for the Cup with Count Chivas, Doriemus and Dupain. Page 68.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Winning the Brazilian Grand Prix was one of the most satisfying experiences of his eight-year career, according to motorcycle champion Mick Doohan. After being forced off the track late in the race, Doohan recovered to take the title from Repsol Honda teammate Alex Criville. Page 53.

After leading the Australian Opals to a bronze basketball medal at the Atlanta Olympics, Sydney Flames guard Michele Timms is likely to reject a US$125,000 one-year deal to play in the newly established ABL, preferring to take up a significantly smaller ofer from the WNBA, which offers more long-term stability. Page 58.

After taking 43 grade wickets last season, Penrith fast bowler Steve Nikitaris has been selected to play in the New South Wales side for Sunday's one-day, Mercantile Mutual cricket match against Western Australia at North Sydney Oval. Page 58.
